icc.estimand: Ratio of the between-model variance component to the sum of the between-model and residual components in a two-way layout with arm fixed effects and one account per model-arm cell, i.e. ICC(3,1) in the Shrout-Fleiss scheme (McGraw and Wong case 3A).
icc.model_effects: Models are treated as random for the purpose of forming the ratio, arms as fixed. The eight models are not a sample from a population of models -- they are the eight the organiser selected -- so the ratio is read as a descriptive partition of variance among these eight implementations and not as an estimate of a population reliability.
icc.interval: Exact F-based interval of Shrout and Fleiss (1979), inverting the distribution of the ratio of mean squares. It is exact under that model's assumptions -- additivity of model and arm effects, normal and homoscedastic residuals -- and not merely because the formula is closed-form.
icc.negative_lower_limit: The interval is computed on the variance-ratio scale and then mapped to the ICC scale. When the model mean square is below the residual mean square the implied between-model variance is negative, and the mapped lower limit is negative with it. A variance cannot be negative; the limit should be read as 'not distinguishable from zero', and it is reported untruncated so that the width of the interval is not misrepresented.
